name: GitHub
oneLiner: No review; new OAuth apps issue 8-hour expiring tokens

review.what: None for an OAuth app; GitHub Marketplace listing is optional

limits.text: OAuth tokens use the user's rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.
A private GitHub App can only be installed on the account that owns it.

requirements.text: Register the app with a name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL.
Use only information you consider public in the app's fields, since users see them.
A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
A GitHub App must be set to 'Any account' (public) before other accounts can install it.

gotchas.text: 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default for new OAuth apps; uncheck it only if your code can't refresh.
Expiring tokens last 8 hours and the refresh token 6 months; each refresh invalidates the old pair.
GitHub App user tokens also expire after 8 hours by default; installation tokens expire after 1 hour.
Non-expiring OAuth tokens are revoked automatically if unused for one year.
Only 10 tokens per user/app/scope are kept; creating an 11th revokes an older one.
New organizations enable OAuth app access restrictions by default, so an org owner must approve your OAuth app.
With a GitHub App, users must install it on their account or org separately; Composio doesn't supply the install link.
OAuth apps act only as a user; GitHub Apps can also act as the app and get finer-grained permissions.

steps.t: Decide between an OAuth app (simpler) and a GitHub App (fine-grained, needs install)
Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App; fill name, homepage and callback URL
Leave 'Expire user access tokens' on, register, then generate and copy a client secret
Create a GitHub OAuth2 auth config in Composio with the client ID, secret and scopes
Connect a test account and, for org repos, ask the org owner to approve the app

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as the authorization callback URL (up to 10 are allowed); use the exact value your Composio auth config shows.

sources.t: Differences between GitHub Apps and OAuth apps
Making a GitHub App public or private

unverified: GitHub's comparison page still calls OAuth app tokens long-lived by default, while the creation page says expiry is on by default for new apps.

name: Linear
oneLiner: No review to use; access tokens expire after 24 hours

review.what: None to use the app; listing in Linear's integration directory is an optional form submission

limits.text: OAuth apps get 5,000 requests and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour per user or app user.

requirements.text: Configure your redirect callback URLs on the app; the token exchange must use the same redirect_uri.
Linear highly recommends creating a dedicated workspace to own the OAuth app.
Directory listings are for useful integrations built by formal companies, not hobby or low-effort apps.
A directory listing needs a submission form, 320x320 color and white icons, and 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000.

gotchas.text: Authorization-code access tokens are valid for 24 hours and come with a refresh token.
All OAuth apps were moved to the refresh token system on April 1, 2026.
Each refresh returns a new access and refresh token; a lost response can be replayed within 30 minutes.
actor=app creates resources as the app instead of the authorizing user.
Request the admin scope only when absolutely necessary.
Every admin of the workspace that owns the app can access the app's settings.

steps.t: Create (or pick) a dedicated Linear workspace to own the app
Create an OAuth2 application at linear.app/settings/api/applications/new
Add the Composio callback URL and copy the client ID and secret
Create a Linear OAuth2 auth config in Composio with your credentials and trimmed scopes
Connect a test workspace and confirm token refresh works after 24 hours

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as a callback URL; use the exact value your Composio auth config shows.
unverified: Linear's own docs don't describe the 'Public' toggle that third-party guides say is needed for other workspaces to authorize the app.
Integration directory review time is not published.

name: Jira
oneLiner: Private until you share it; unreviewed apps show a warning

review.what: Optional Atlassian approval via a third-party integration listing on the Marketplace; without it users see a warning

limits.text: Before sharing: a new 3LO app is private, so only you can install and use it.
Before approval: users installing an unapproved integration are warned it hasn't been reviewed by Atlassian.
Sharing doesn't list the app on the Marketplace; you must send the authorization URL to every user.

requirements.text: Create an 'OAuth 2.0 integration' in the developer console, configure OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and add Jira API scopes under Permissions.
Turn on 'Enable sharing' under Distribution before anyone else can authorize the app.
Apps that store personal data must report those account IDs to the Personal data reporting API.
Report each stored account at least every 7 days by default, or per the Cycle-Period header.
Erase or refresh a user's data when the reporting API says so; 3LO apps call POST https://api.atlassian.com/app/report-accounts/.
For Marketplace approval, give reviewers access to a test instance of your software.

gotchas.text: Add offline_access to the scope to get a refresh token at all.
Refresh tokens rotate; store the new one every time, since the old one is disabled.
A refresh token expires after 90 days of inactivity, and then the user must re-authorize.
Changing scopes forces users who already consented to consent again.
API calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}; get the cloudid from accessible-resources.
Site-scoped grants make users pick one site per consent, so multi-site installs mean repeating the flow.
Admins can't revoke one user's grant from Connected Apps; they can only uninstall the app.
Jira 3LO apps can't declare searchable entity properties, so they can't be used in JQL.

steps.t: In developer.atlassian.com > Developer console, create an OAuth 2.0 integration
Authorization > OAuth 2.0 (3LO) > Configure; paste the Composio callback URL
Permissions: add the Jira API (and User Identity API) and pick classic or granular scopes
Decide whether you store Atlassian account IDs and draft the personal data reporting job if so
Distribution: enable sharing, then copy client ID and secret from Settings
Create the Jira OAuth2 auth config in Composio with offline_access in the scopes

callbackNote: Set the 3LO callback URL to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback; use the exact value your Composio auth config shows.

sources.t: User privacy guide for app developers
List a third-party integration on the Marketplace

unverified: The exact fields of the Distribution form (vendor name, privacy policy, personal data declaration) aren't listed in Atlassian's public docs; only third-party and community sources describe them.
Marketplace approval time for 3LO integrations is not published.
Access token lifetime isn't stated; the token response gives it in expires_in.
Composio's toolkit page says managed OAuth is available, but composio.dev/auth/jira says Composio does not provide managed Jira credentials.

name: Figma
oneLiner: Public apps need Figma approval before outside users

review.what: Figma review of a public OAuth app (testing instructions, reviewer access)
review.wait: not stated; Figma says it varies with volume

limits.text: Before publishing: a draft app can only be tested by you and your plan's admins.
Before approval: a private app only works for users in the team or org it belongs to.

requirements.text: The app must be associated with a team or organization; its users don't need to belong to it.
Public apps need testing instructions and any trial access or login credentials the reviewer needs.
Apps need an accurate name, description and an icon that matches your brand.
Provide a support contact and keep it accurate.
Apps must not bulk-export file content or index files through the projects endpoints.
Users must authorize in a web browser; WebViews are not supported.

gotchas.text: The client secret is shown only once when you create the app.
Any change to a published public app needs another review.
files:read and file_read are deprecated; apps must use granular scopes.
Existing apps marked 'Update required' must be republished to meet the November 17, 2025 rules.
Write scopes like teams:write and folders:write work only in private apps on Enterprise.
file_variables:read and :write are Enterprise-only scopes.
Authorization codes expire after 30 seconds.
Access tokens last 90 days; refreshing invalidates the previous token because Figma keeps one per user per app.
OAuth rate limits are tracked per user, per plan, per app.
Users on View or Collab seats get up to 20 Tier 1 file requests a month, possibly fewer under load.

steps.t: Go to figma.com/developers/apps and create an app under your team or org; save the client secret
OAuth credentials: add the Composio redirect URL; OAuth scopes: pick granular scopes
Create the Figma OAuth2 auth config in Composio with the same scopes
Draft reviewer testing instructions, privacy policy and support contact
Publish privately to test with your org, then submit as public for review

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback on the app's OAuth credentials page; use the exact value your Composio auth config shows.
unverified: Figma does not publish a review duration.
The review guidelines page covers 'Figma Community Apps'; it's not explicit that every item applies to REST API OAuth apps.

name: Notion
oneLiner: Reconnecting a user can kill their old refresh token

review.what: None found to use a public integration; a security review applies only to Marketplace listing (unconfirmed)

requirements.text: Set the integration type to Public to use OAuth; internal integrations only use an API token.
Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, match exactly, and have no trailing slash, fragment or wildcard.
Users pick which pages to share during authorization, then press Allow access.

gotchas.text: Notion has no OAuth scopes; access comes from the pages and databases users share.
Actions show the integration's name and logo, not the user's; your own app lets you set them.
Connecting the same user again issues a new token pair and can invalidate the older refresh token.
Keep one connection per real user per Notion app to avoid broken refresh tokens.
A user removing the connection in Settings > Connections revokes the tokens.
On Enterprise, workspace owners can restrict which connections members may install.
With your own app, Notion webhooks need you to paste back a verification token Notion sends to Composio.

steps.t: Open notion.so/profile/integrations and create a new integration in your workspace
Name it, pick the associated workspace and set the type to Public
Add the Composio redirect URI and pick capabilities (read, update, insert, user info)
Copy the OAuth client ID and client secret
Create the Notion OAuth2 auth config in Composio with your credentials

callbackNote: Add Composio's redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback under OAuth domains & URIs; it must match exactly with no trailing slash.
unverified: developers.notion.com could not be reached from this environment, so Notion's own developer docs were not read.
Search snippets say public connections need a Notion security review only to be listed on the Marketplace.
Search snippets say installation scope (any workspace vs selected workspaces) is fixed at creation and only 'any workspace' can be listed.
Which fields (privacy policy, terms of use, company details) are mandatory for a public integration was not confirmed.
Notion's access token lifetime was not confirmed.
